name: Executive Summary
description: Sponsor-facing 7-slide deck. Engine fills cover + numeric stats; AI writes the three narrative panels (headline findings, top risks, executive recommendations) so the sponsor reads curated prose, not raw bullet dumps. **Hard constraint:** every section lands in a fixed-height slide text frame (≈3.5" × 11"). The total budget per section is ~600 characters across no more than 5 bullets. Going over makes PowerPoint auto-shrink the text to illegible sizes — keep it tight.

sections.title: Headline findings
sections.purpose:
Up to 5 most material findings for an executive sponsor.

**Strict format:**
- Markdown bullet list, NO sub-bullets.
- Each bullet: ONE sentence, ≤ 18 words.
- Lead with the issue in 2-4 words (optionally bold), then the business consequence.
- NO domain/severity prefixes like `[CRITICAL/security_iam]`.
- NO supporting paragraphs, NO follow-up sentences.

Total output ≤ 600 characters. Cut the long tail aggressively — the engineering audience sees the full list elsewhere. Order by severity then by business impact.

sections.title: Top risks
sections.purpose:
Up to 5 most material risks. Skip LOW severity.

**Strict format:**
- Markdown bullet list, NO sub-bullets.
- Each bullet: ONE sentence, ≤ 22 words. Pattern: `**Risk title** — impact in plain language; mitigation in a clause.`
- NO category-code prefixes.

Total output ≤ 700 characters. The slide text frame is fixed-height — exceeding the budget makes PowerPoint shrink the text to unreadable sizes.

sections.title: Priority recommendations
sections.purpose:
Up to 5 priority recommendations the sponsor should approve next.

**Strict format:**
- Markdown bullet list, NO sub-bullets.
- Each bullet: ONE sentence, ≤ 20 words. Pattern: `**Action verb opener** — outcome unlocked; effort hint if defensible.`
- Synthesise — do NOT paste the raw recommendations list.
- NO priority/domain prefixes.

Total output ≤ 650 characters. Cluster by theme only if it actually saves words.
